origin: Owner-requested scope in the 2026-09-19 implementation conversation
outcome: Reduce unnecessary generative-model tokens and elapsed time in Pi and Tau by using native Jev typed decisions for intent/capability, skills, bounded tool proposals and useful Memory/code evidence, without weakening task success, data boundaries, freshness, evidence authority or human checkpoints.

architecture.pi: Native TypeScript extension and library; no Python subprocess for Jev calls
architecture.tau: Native Python package and typed registration decorator; no Node dependency
architecture.shared: Versioned question definitions, strict decision semantics, schemas and conformance fixtures
architecture.memory: Shared service owns retrieval, ingest-code projection, grounded routing and QRA state
architecture.monitor_skills: Catalog qualification/version evidence and drift feedback, not live quota guesses
architecture.executor: Pi/Tau retain policy, source checks, capacity reservation, execution and completion authority

acceptance.requirement: Native Python and TypeScript agree on decisions and bindings for shared valid, malformed, uncertain and denied fixtures.
Complete-payload egress checks precede hosted calls; restricted/unknown data does not silently reach Jev or a hosted fallback.
Pi reads scoped ingest-code evidence through Memory, retains source identity and uncertainty, and never presents indexing or relevance as current-source repair proof.
Skill selection preserves explicit requests, required contracts and qualified version evidence; missing/broken skills are distinguished from semantic no-match.
Intent/capability judgment is separate from deterministic model eligibility, cost, context fit, live rate/capacity admission and user pins.
Tool candidates have validated bound arguments; the owner rechecks state/schema/policy and produces independent execution receipts.
Memory answer/clarify/deflect/draft semantics remain shared; implementation work continues after informational recall and genuine human/QRA checkpoints cannot be silently approved.
Installed Pi, headless/subagent sessions and Tau integration pass cancellation, replay, version drift, no-match and dependency-failure canaries.
On retained matched workloads, main-model token use and end-to-end elapsed time improve over the deterministic-cleanup baseline, including Jev overhead, caches, queues and retries.
The same matched workloads retain required evidence and independently verified success; no savings claim relies only on character counts or model self-reported completion.

completion_rule: MET requires retained evidence for every acceptance ID, including live integrations and matched-task efficacy. Offline tests alone cannot satisfy the goal.
change_rule: Changes to this target require explicit owner authorization, a new revision and preserved prior goal evidence; agents may not weaken it to match implementation.
